objective: Harden browser-harness by making each critical runtime, data, packaging, and skill surface explicit, testable, and small enough to improve without adding a manager layer.

surfaces.scope: browser-harness command execution, setup/doctor/update flags, and stdin or -c code execution.
contracts: ensure_daemon runs before user code execution
first navigation guidance remains new_tab(url), not goto_url(url)
run.py stays a thin command shim
risks: stale daemon treated as healthy
user active tab clobbered by default navigation
CLI grows into an unreviewable control layer
surfaces.positive_probe: Run CLI/unit tests that prove ensure_daemon is invoked before exec and setup/doctor/update flags route to admin helpers.
surfaces.negative_probe: Search the CLI for manager-style subcommand/control abstractions and for default navigation patterns that contradict SKILL.md.

reachability.validation: flag parsing and mutually exclusive setup/doctor/update/code paths
reachability.routing: run.py dispatches to admin helpers or executes helper-preloaded code
reachability.state_effect: may start/reuse daemon; no browser navigation unless user code requests it
reachability.output: stdout/stderr from selected command or executed snippet
reachability.lifecycle: daemon start is delegated to admin.ensure_daemon
reachability.observability: daemon startup errors surface with /tmp/bh-<name>.log hint
reachability.regression: test_cli_entrypoint coverage should exercise flag routing and exec ordering

surfaces.scope: Daemon startup, endpoint discovery, Unix socket/pid/log files, stale process recovery, and shutdown cleanup.
contracts: CDP endpoints default to loopback only
endpoint URLs must not contain credentials
stale daemon sockets are probed with a real CDP call
restart cleans current bh-* paths and legacy bu-* paths
risks: unsafe remote CDP attachment
credential-bearing endpoint logs
dead daemon accepts socket connections but cannot control Chrome
pid/socket cleanup targets the wrong process
surfaces.positive_probe: Unit tests cover endpoint validation, DevToolsActivePort resolution, daemon_alive probing, and restart cleanup.
surfaces.negative_probe: Remote or credentialed CDP endpoints fail unless explicitly allowed and redacted.

reachability.routing: env BH_CDP_WS wins, otherwise DevToolsActivePort discovery
reachability.state_effect: creates/updates socket, pid, log, and in-memory event buffer
reachability.output: newline-delimited JSON responses to helper client
reachability.lifecycle: startup, stale recovery, shutdown, pid/socket unlink
reachability.regression: test_daemon.py and test_admin.py should cover validation and cleanup paths

surfaces.scope: helpers.py socket client, raw CDP request/response handling, reconnect behavior, and recoverable session errors.
contracts: mutating CDP methods are not automatically retried after socket errors
non-mutating requests may reconnect once
oversized, malformed, or timeout responses poison the socket and force reconnect
recoverable target/session errors retry once after reconnect
risks: duplicate click/navigation/file-upload side effects
socket stream misalignment after malformed response
silent stale-session failure
surfaces.positive_probe: Unit tests simulate reconnects, mutating send failures, malformed responses, and recoverable CDP target errors.
surfaces.negative_probe: A mutating method failure must not be retried by _send.

reachability.validation: _send validates JSON response and CDP error payload
reachability.routing: all helper CDP calls flow through _send unless explicitly documented
reachability.execution: Unix socket request to daemon relay
reachability.state_effect: may reconnect helper socket; may mutate browser only once for mutating CDP
reachability.output: CDP result dict or loud RuntimeError
reachability.lifecycle: socket opened lazily, closed on atexit or corruption
reachability.observability: error message includes method for mutating socket failures

surfaces.scope: new_tab/goto_url/load waits, meaningful content readiness, blank renders, and stale/internal tab recovery.
contracts: extraction workflows use wait_for_content rather than fixed sleep or load-only readiness
internal/stale tabs are recoverable with ensure_real_tab
blocked or blank pages are not treated as empty data
risks: running extraction JS on a challenge shell
declaring empty results from a page that never rendered
operating on an internal Chrome tab
surfaces.positive_probe: Readiness tests cover useful text, timeout, blank content, and stale tab recovery.
surfaces.negative_probe: A WAF/auth/blank page must produce blocked or unobservable status before extraction.

reachability.routing: navigation helpers call load waits then content checks when extraction is expected
reachability.execution: Page.navigate or Target.createTarget plus Runtime content inspection
reachability.state_effect: active target may change; page content status is sampled
reachability.lifecycle: waits bounded by timeout and stale session recovery
reachability.observability: block reason and content lengths in returned status

surfaces.scope: WAF, bot-detection, auth gate, login redirect, and Turnstile handling boundaries.
contracts: detect blocks and auth gates before extraction
authorized recovery paths only
persistent block emits __UNOBSERVABLE__
no fingerprinting or WAF circumvention guidance
risks: mistaking security shell for data
unsafe cookie/token extraction into standalone clients
normal content false-positive blocked
surfaces.positive_probe: Fixtures cover Kasada, Akamai, Cloudflare, generic WAF, auth gate, and normal content.
surfaces.negative_probe: Normal content with benign WAF-looking strings must not be blocked.

reachability.routing: blocked status routes to recovery, stop, or unobservable output
reachability.execution: pure content inspection plus optional browser-native Turnstile interaction
reachability.state_effect: no standalone secret extraction or hidden bypass state
reachability.lifecycle: bounded wait and explicit stop rule when authorized recovery fails

surfaces.scope: Authenticated browser profile reuse, redacted manifests, private auth bundles, same-domain cookie headers, and restore verification.
contracts: the user's browser profile is the primary auth store
raw cookies/storage belong only in ignored private paths when explicitly requested
redacted manifests record names, domains, receipts, and verification context
restore proof requires a fresh profile or separate process
risks: committed session secrets
same-profile restore false positive
cross-origin cookie leakage
surfaces.positive_probe: Tests cover redaction, cookie URL matching, manifest fields, same-domain headers, and restore failure on login redirect.
surfaces.negative_probe: Secret-like cookie/storage values must not appear in committed manifests, fixtures, receipts, or package artifacts.

reachability.validation: origin, cookie domain/path/secure matching, redaction scans
reachability.routing: browser profile -> redacted manifest or ignored private bundle
reachability.execution: CDP cookie/storage reads and optional restore into supplied client
reachability.state_effect: local manifest/private bundle only when requested
reachability.output: redacted manifest, capability receipt, or restored-state verification result
reachability.observability: cookie names/domains, storage keys, and receipt refs without values

surfaces.scope: fetch(source=auto/http/session/browser), HTTP helpers, browser-session HTTP, source receipts, and fallback decisions.
contracts: exports and structured APIs are preferred when complete
field-level parity decides canonical source
fallback reason and capability receipt are recorded for serious workflows
browser extraction fills gaps rather than duplicating every field by default
risks: page-level success hides missing fields
silent fallback to weaker source
session HTTP used before browser profile is seeded
surfaces.positive_probe: Tests should prove source fallback order, browser-session seeding requirement, and Response helper behavior.
surfaces.negative_probe: A lightweight backend cannot become canonical for private/authenticated fields without a capability receipt.

reachability.validation: source parameter, content status, field parity, receipt presence
reachability.routing: http -> session -> browser fallback for auto where allowed
reachability.execution: urllib HTTP, browser-session HTTP, or browser navigation
reachability.state_effect: may seed browser session; may create receipt in domain-local store
reachability.output: Response object plus optional capability receipt
reachability.lifecycle: fallback stops on blocks or missing authorization
reachability.observability: source, status, fields found/missing, fallback reason
reachability.regression: test_helpers.py fetch/source tests and domain receipt tests

surfaces.scope: CDP Network event capture, response body capture, endpoint clustering, replay, and API promotion.
contracts: body capture is opt-in
smart_wait/network_idle must not drain events during active capture
headers/bodies must be redacted before committed receipts
captured API promotion requires replay/schema parity
risks: event stream stolen by another wait
committed Authorization/Cookie headers or private bodies
promoting an API endpoint from a non-replayable browser-only request
surfaces.positive_probe: Tests cover start/poll/stop, max_entries, body capture opt-in, replay summaries, and redaction fixtures.
surfaces.negative_probe: NetworkCapture receipts must reject raw cookie, authorization, bearer, and session headers.

reachability.validation: active capture state, max entries, request method, content-type/status parity
reachability.routing: CDP Network events -> in-memory entries -> endpoint clusters/replay
reachability.state_effect: in-memory capture only unless caller writes redacted receipt
reachability.output: endpoint list, response pairs, replay summary
reachability.lifecycle: start, poll, stop, clear; no overlapping event drains
reachability.observability: summary counts by resource type/status and pending requests

surfaces.scope: CrawlState dedupe/saturation/accounting and SafetyGate request/time/block/429 budgets.
contracts: long crawls have a key field and dedupe accounting
bounded crawls enforce request/time/block budgets
blocked pages are recorded separately from empty result pages
saturation claims include marginal discovery evidence
risks: infinite or overbroad crawl
duplicate records inflate coverage
blocked pages counted as complete
premature saturation from too-short marginal window
surfaces.positive_probe: Tests cover add/dedupe, blocked records, scope totals, save/load, saturation, unseen estimate, and SafetyGate limits.
surfaces.negative_probe: A crawl with blocked pages or unknown key fields cannot claim full coverage.

reachability.validation: key_field, request budget, elapsed budget, block threshold, status code
reachability.routing: domain workflow checks gate before requests and state after page/entity extraction
reachability.execution: in-memory accounting plus optional JSON save/load
reachability.state_effect: records, occurrence counts, blocked list, marginal counts
reachability.output: summary, saved JSON, or raised RuntimeError when configured
reachability.observability: records, deduped, blocked, scope totals, saturated, estimated_unseen

surfaces.scope: Browser and parser extraction field semantics, selector probes, primary keys, fixtures, and coverage triage.
contracts: fields distinguish value, confirmed absent, __UNOBSERVABLE__, and not checked
selectors are probed before extractor code is trusted
primary key fields must not be all-null on representative pages
surface maps include positive and negative probes
risks: silent data loss through empty strings
wrong entity type queried
selector drift masked by sparse results
fixtures only cover development examples
surfaces.positive_probe: Extractor tests include fixture-backed value, absent, unobservable, and omitted-key cases.
surfaces.negative_probe: A blocked page fixture must not pass as an empty but successful extraction.

reachability.entry: domain extractor scripts, parser helpers, and extraction JS snippets
reachability.validation: selector probes, entity type, primary key, four-state field semantics
reachability.routing: source discovery chooses parser/API/UI path before extraction
reachability.execution: Response parser, JS extraction, or domain script parser
reachability.state_effect: CSV/JSON/report rows with provenance and field states
reachability.observability: fill-rate triage, broken selector list, source receipt
reachability.regression: domain parser fixtures and surface-map tests

surfaces.scope: Root router, domain index, packaged domain assets, surface maps, and empirical skill promotion.
contracts: known domains route to overview.md or the most specific file
domain skills contain durable rules, not task narration or secrets
rich domain bundles expose surface maps, fixtures, receipts, and scripts when applicable
empirical lessons pass the learning gate before promotion
risks: packaged install cannot discover domain skills
skill prose captures private/session-specific state
generalizable mechanics duplicated inside domain docs
surfaces.positive_probe: Tests prove packaged domain skill discovery and surface-map contract validity.
surfaces.negative_probe: Private/generated directories must be excluded from reusable guidance and package artifacts.

reachability.entry: SKILL.md router and domain-skills/README.md cold start
reachability.validation: domain folder, overview/readme presence, surface-map schema
reachability.routing: root skill -> domain skill -> interaction skill for mechanics
reachability.execution: agent reads skill files and optional scripts/assets
reachability.state_effect: no runtime state unless scripts are explicitly run
reachability.output: operator guidance, script commands, fixtures, receipts
reachability.lifecycle: empirical learning gate and index updates
reachability.observability: surface maps, tests, and package discovery checks
reachability.regression: test_helpers packaged asset discovery and skill-learning tests

surfaces.scope: data_display.py generated HTML reports, assets, disabled states, and browser-visible render checks.
contracts: report HTML renders data without overlapping or missing controls
disabled reasons and missing data are explicit
assets load from source and packaged installs
runtime verification covers representative desktop/mobile views when UI changes
risks: static tests pass while browser UI is broken
missing/private/unobservable data appears as empty success
packaged asset paths differ from repo paths
surfaces.positive_probe: Fixture render tests plus browser screenshot/pixel checks for significant UI changes.
surfaces.negative_probe: Missing/private/unobservable fields must not render as ordinary empty values.

reachability.entry: data_display.py APIs and domain scripts that emit reports
reachability.validation: schema/field metadata, disabled reasons, asset paths
reachability.state_effect: local HTML artifact only when user requests report output
reachability.lifecycle: asset cleanup and no generated reports committed unless intended
reachability.observability: render screenshots or fixture HTML assertions

surfaces.scope: pyproject package config, wheel contents, clean install smoke, console scripts, package data, and artifact exclusions.
contracts: runtime modules and skill/assets packages are included
private/generated/session/cache artifacts are excluded
console scripts work after wheel install
packaged domain skill discovery matches source checkout behavior
risks: structural pyproject test passes but wheel omits files
private data leaks into distribution
entrypoint works only in editable checkout
surfaces.positive_probe: Build wheel, inspect archive, install into temp env, smoke browser-harness help/doctor-safe import paths.
surfaces.negative_probe: Wheel content scan finds no .private-data, .session-store, outputs, downloads, cookies, HARs, or profile state.

reachability.validation: wheel archive inventory and clean-env import checks
reachability.execution: build backend creates wheel; installed script imports run:main
reachability.output: wheel file, installed console scripts, package data
reachability.observability: captured wheel inventory and smoke command output

surfaces.scope: Repo-native verification commands, hygiene scans, optional live/E2E gates, and session close checks.
contracts: default gate uses uv sync --group dev and uv run --group dev pytest -q
plugin-conflict fallback disables pytest plugin autoload
live/E2E tests remain gated by explicit environment variables
final session leaves no unrelated generated junk
risks: agents run host-only checks that miss packaged behavior
live tests run unintentionally against external services
verification leaves large generated artifacts
surfaces.positive_probe: Documented gate runs locally and records command, cwd, exit code, and decisive output.
surfaces.negative_probe: Quality gate must not require external credentials or live sites unless an explicit env flag is set.

reachability.entry: README development commands and CI/local gate docs
reachability.validation: dependency setup, pytest collection, env-gated live tests
reachability.routing: static/unit/package checks before optional live/E2E checks
reachability.output: pass/fail summaries and captured decisive errors
reachability.regression: documented quality gate checked by tests where practical

borrowed_patterns.adapt: opt-in traces and reproducible receipts for failed or high-risk runs
borrowed_patterns.reject: large always-on framework around the thin harness

borrowed_patterns.adapt: field contracts, item validation, and source provenance
borrowed_patterns.reject: crawler framework replacement for direct browser-harness scripts

borrowed_patterns.adapt: stale-pane guards, profile identity checks, halt detection, saturation/dedupe ledgers, and selector-drift fixtures
borrowed_patterns.reject: private API token reuse, stealth/proxy defaults, lock-file deletion, and raw profile/session artifacts
